headline: Trump meets Xi at the plane. The truce runs to January.
summary: Xi Jinping landed at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday evening and Trump met him on the tarmac, with two B-1 bombers overhead and a 100ft red carpet. No president had welcomed a foreign leader at the base since Kennedy met Macmillan in 1962. The same day Treasury extended the US-China trade truce to January. A state dinner follows Thursday.

cover_question.q: Why did Trump go to the airport?

cover_answer: To show respect. Xi skipped Trump's plane in May.
table_question: Should you be extra polite to someone you're about to bargain with?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The leader of China flew to America yesterday, and our president went to the airport to meet his plane, the way you meet a grandparent at the gate instead of waiting at home. Two big jets flew over and a band played. They'll talk for three days about buying and selling things. Nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: Meeting someone at the gate is a thing they've done. The jets and the band are the picture. Say what happened, not what it means.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old reasons from what they have seen, so the script gives them the airport gate, a grandparent's welcome, jets and a band, and leaves the trade truce to older kids. One vivid picture stands in for the whole visit. Expect "are China and America friends?" They argue a lot and trade a lot, and this week they're polite.

8-12.script: In May Trump flew to Beijing and Xi didn't meet his plane. Wednesday Trump went to the airport for Xi: red carpet, two B-1 bombers, a band. Each side keeps score on respect like a scoreboard. Same day, they stretched their trade truce to January: some US tariffs stay low, China sells rare earths.
8-12.why: A snub in May, a red carpet in September. That's the scoreboard.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script gives them the ledger: Xi skipped the plane in May, Trump went to the plane in September. The scoreboard is a mechanism they run at school every day. Then the truce, a give on each side. Expect "what happens in January?" Nobody knows. That's what the three days are for.

13-17.script: Why roll out the red carpet for a rival? Trump wants deals: lower Chinese tariffs, more rare earths, more farm exports, and China backed out of the last two before. Second: 57% of Americans favor cooperating with China, but 63% of Trump's own base wants less. Who is the show for?
13-17.why: A bet his own base doesn't want. Let them work out who the show is for.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: the welcome is a bid for deals China has walked away from before, and 63% of Trump's own base would rather he kept his distance. The script hands them both and asks who the show is for. Expect "does this stuff actually work?" Say you don't know, and that January is the test.

5-7.q: Why did Trump go to the airport?
5-7.a: To be extra welcoming. Meeting someone at the gate instead of waiting at home says they matter. In May, Xi didn't do it for him.

8-12.a: A pause in the fight over taxes on each other's goods.
Honor and muscle at once. The B-1 is a main US combat jet.

13-17.q: Why the red carpet for a rival?
13-17.a: Deals: tariffs, rare earths, farm exports. China reneged before.
57% of Americans want cooperation. 63% of Trump's base want less.
